entries.n: From Old English, meaning to form, make, effect.
From French franc. Wright says it is used in its literal sense of "freely".
Wright says it is the root of "affray", of which "afraid" is the participle; still common as a provincialism.
Wright links it to a word for devouring, as a beast eats; hence to corrode like an ulcerous sore, or eat away like a moth.
The ending -ly is adverbial here, as well as adjectival.
In Hebrew the word means bands. The Jews wrote texts on pieces of parchment made into a packet, taking these verses literally.
From Old English; the opposite of "toward".
